decisions.title: Remove Axon Framework in favour of plain Spring events and direct handler calls
decisions.decision: Axon command/query/event gateways and annotations were removed. Integration events are published with Spring's ApplicationEventPublisher and consumed with @Async/@EventListener, and controllers and event handlers call command/query handlers directly.
decisions.reason: Part of the 'Framework independence' roadmap item. The data does not state why Axon specifically was dropped (for example, the cost of the Axon 5 API migration).

remove commandGateway

framework independence

decisions.title: Adopt Axon Framework for command/query dispatch and event handling (later reverted)
decisions.decision: Handlers were marked with Axon annotations. Controllers used CommandGateway/QueryGateway instead of calling handlers directly, and integration events moved from Spring @EventListener to Axon EventBus/@EventHandler.
decisions.reason: To avoid writing custom DDD building block classes, and to get Axon's event publishing and event sourcing functionality.

Axon Framework is used as DDD library for not creating custom building block classes.
more functionality for event publishing/event sourcing is used from Axon functionality

decisions.title: Modular monolith with DDD bounded contexts
decisions.decision: The single user-management app was restructured into a multi-project Gradle build. Each bounded context is a separate module (administration, courses, course-enrollments, course-reviews, users) plus common/web/configuration/security modules.
decisions.reason: Intended as an example modular monolith with DDD that can later be moved to microservices.

evidence.quote: - parent gradle project settings; - user service module; - remove not actual changes;
Example of Modular Monolith Java application with Domain-Driven Design.
In the plans, this application will be moved to microservices architecture.

support.why: Quotes say example modular monolith with DDD, planned move to microservices

decisions.title: Asynchronous, data-replicating communication between bounded contexts
decisions.decision: Bounded contexts communicate only through asynchronous integration events. They do not share data or transactions, and each context keeps its own local copies of related concepts (Teacher, Student, Reviewer, ReviewableCourse, EnrollCourse).
decisions.reason: Data replication reduces coupling between bounded contexts and increases their independence.

evidence.quote: Communication between bounded contexts is asynchronous. Bounded contexts don't share data, it's forbidden to create a transaction which spans more than one bounded context.
This solution reduces coupling of bounded contexts through data replication across contexts which results to higher bounded contexts independence.
- user created integration event; - command handler for courses module; - teacher model with repo;
evidence.rejected: no such commit (or ambiguous short id)

support.why: Quote explicitly says replication reduces coupling, increases independence

decisions.title: Simple CQRS: command handlers for writes, DTO queries for reads
decisions.decision: Service classes were replaced by command handlers that run full aggregate logic on writes. Query handlers build DTOs directly with JPQL constructor expressions on reads.
alternatives: Classic service layer returning entities/DTOs for both reads and writes
decisions.reason: Gives flexibility to optimize the model separately for read and write operations.

decisions.title: Command handlers may return generated identifiers
decisions.decision: Create-style command handlers return the new resource's UUID.
alternatives: Strict CQRS where commands return nothing
